findings.title: READ issued to a bank one cycle after that bank was PRECHARGEd (no ACTIVATE between)
findings.requirement: After PRE to bank b, no RD/WR to b until an ACT to b (JESD79-3 bank state machine).
findings.expected: After PRE to bank b, no RD/WR to b until an ACT to b (JESD79-3 bank state machine).
findings.actual: PRE b=1 at cycle 183, RD b=1 at cycle 184.
findings.mechanism: JasperGold counterexample, 136 cycles from reset under a protocol-legal host: cycle 183 PRE bank 1 (A10=0), cycle 184 RD bank 1 col 0. The generated PROTO_001 tracker (row-open state from the observed ACT/PRE stream) shows bank 1 closed when the READ is issued. Never observed in simulation (no path stimulus reaches this interleaving); the scheduler or its bank_tracker gating lets a CAS follow its own precharge. Likely the same root as the open scheduler re-grant defect (commands are also held for 2-3 consecutive cycles in the trace, i.e. re-issued). [found on drop 1fea117; awaiting formal re-prove on a82f2070de32]

repro.assumptions: none beyond CSR/status tie-offs; host Wishbone inputs free and, in the trace, protocol-legal

findings.title: scheduler: REF_001
findings.requirement: Refresh postpone count exceeded max_postpone_count (spec: controller_architecture.refresh_policy.max_postpone_count). Judged on refresh_level.state, the controller's own levels emitted on every change: a violation when pending > max_postpone_count, or when starve = 1. refresh_req carries only the rising edge of ref_required and its pending field is the count at that edge; it must NOT be used to judge this rule. A count equal to max_postpone_count is legal (the design saturates there).
findings.expected: Refresh postpone count exceeded max_postpone_count (spec: controller_architecture.refresh_policy.max_postpone_count). Judged on refresh_level.state, the controller's own levels emitted on every change: a violation when pending > max_postpone_count, or when starve = 1. refresh_req carries only the rising edge of ref_required and its pending field is the count at that edge; it must NOT be used to judge this rule. A count equal to max_postpone_count is legal (the design saturates there).

findings.title: scheduler: SCHED_003
findings.requirement: A refresh request must be serviced: once refresh_req.request has been seen, at least one REFRESH command must follow before the end of the trace. Judged at final(): a violation when a request was seen and NO REFRESH was ever issued. The level stream refresh_level.state (pending count) is NOT a request counter for this rule: the count rises on every tREFI tick and the trace may end with refreshes legitimately pending inside their postpone budget, so a non-zero pending count at the end of the trace is not a violation (REF_001 owns the budget). Count requests only on refresh_req.request; count service only on REFRESH commands.

findings.title: PRECHARGE issued one cycle after a WRITE to the same bank (tWR violated; write data lost)
findings.requirement: WR to bank b then no PRE to b for tWR (2 free cycles at 5 ns).
findings.expected: WR to bank b then no PRE to b for tWR (2 free cycles at 5 ns).
findings.actual: WR b=4 at cycle 173, PRE b=4 at cycle 174.
findings.mechanism: JasperGold counterexample, 136 cycles from reset under a protocol-legal host: cycle 173 WR bank 4, cycle 174 PRE bank 4. tWR = 15 ns = 3 controller cycles, so 2 cycles must separate the last write beat from the precharge. Not observed in simulation. bank_tracker's write-recovery timer (cfg_tWR_nCK) does not gate bank_pre_allowed for the cycle after a write, or the scheduler ignores it on the row-conflict path. [found on drop 1fea117; awaiting formal re-prove on a82f2070de32]
